messages:
jen: Heads up — we're seeing a wave of preemptible GPU evictions in us-west2. Preemptible pool (gpu-preempt) available capacity dropped ~30% in the last 8m, short-gen p95 latency spiked. ops-bot alerted at +2m.

arjun: on it. grabbing recent eviction traces and spot-price history. any customer-facing errors yet?

ops-bot: [ALERT] preemptible-eviction-wave detected in us-west2 (gpu-preempt). affected: 73 nodes. time: 2026-03-18T11:33:02Z.

maria: seeing elevated 503s on /v1/generate for a subset of customers on us-west2, mainly short requests. fallback to model-variant is happening but latency still up.

jen: exact numbers from node side:```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-preempt -o wide
# before: 240 Ready
# now: 167 Ready, 73 Terminating/NotReady
```

arjun: spot price telemetry shows sudden bid spikes across instances around 11:28Z -> likely cloud-side reclaiming. I pushed a quick query: `select count(*) from instance_events where reason = 'preemption' and region='us-west2' and time > now() - 15m` returns 73.

leo: recommend immediate mitigations: 1) scale up reserved-on-demand pool (gpu-reserved) by +8 nodes for next 30m; 2) throttle batch jobs and reduce prefill; 3) temporarily divert short-gen traffic to us-central1 and europe-west1 via smart-routing.

jen: agreed. dave — can you flip the routing policy to preference=resilience for latency-sensitive routes? that should send short-gen to other regions while we recover.

maria: routing change in progress. patch:```
PATCH /routing/policies/short-gen
{ "preference": "resilience", "fallback_regions": ["us-central1","europe-west1"] }
```

dave: routing change applied. verifying sticky sessions and model compatibility for customers routed out of us-west2. if any incompatibilities, auto-fallback to CPU small models.

arjun: scaling reserved pool: running `cloudctl instance-groups resize gpu-reserved-us-west2 --increase 8 --type on-demand` now. estimated ready ~3-4m. cost impact minimal for 30m insurance; preferable to degrade.

jen: good. also enabling aggressive KV cache warmup on the nodes that remain to reduce cold-kv hits. maria please add a short-term eval to ensure quality not regressing when we route to variants.

maria: adding eval. running quick prompt set against fallback models, looks fine so far (diffs <1% on hallucination checks).

sre-bot: Postmortem hint: tag all affected ephemeral jobs with `eviction-wave-2026-03-18` for later cost/regression analysis.

leo: one more ask — reduce autoscaler cool-down to 30s for reserved group so we can react quicker during this window. arjun/dave ok to approve?

arjun: approved. making the change.

jen: timeline: 00:00 root alert -> routing + scale started -> 00:04 reserved nodes booting -> 00:07 traffic rebalanced -> 00:10 p95 latency returning toward normal. keep monitoring for another 30m.

maria: customer impact table updated in incident doc: small % latency increase, ~4 customers saw transient 5xxs, self-healed. linking logs: https://redwood-infra.logs/evictions/1913456789

jen: thanks all. post-incident action items: (1) run chaos test for preemption at 20% to validate fallback, (2) evaluate adding a small on-demand insurance buffer in us-west2 (cost vs SLAs), (3) tune routing health checks to detect region preemption earlier. tagging @oncall for follow-up.

dave: marking this thread resolved for now. reopen if we see another wave. :thumbsup:
